findings.title: Mutable container image receives credential-bearing Claude configuration with unrestricted egress
findings.what: The default image uses the mutable `latest` tag, then the launcher mounts the user's entire `~/.claude` directory and `~/.claude.json` read-only into that image. Read-only mounting prevents modification but not disclosure, and the container has no network isolation. A compromised or replaced image can therefore read subscription OAuth credentials or other secrets stored with Claude state and exfiltrate them, violating the stated ADR 0008 boundary.
findings.fix: Pin the default image by immutable digest and expose only an allowlisted, credential-free history projection instead of mounting `~/.claude` or `~/.claude.json` wholesale. Run the dashboard without outbound network access, or through an explicitly allowlisted proxy, after any required image pull.
findings.acceptance: A launcher-level test must inspect the final container arguments and prove that the image reference contains an immutable digest, neither `~/.claude` nor `~/.claude.json` is mounted, credential files cannot be read from the container, and an outbound request from the running container is denied while dashboard history loading still works.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read the cited baseline lines at c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba. The hardening flags at lines 181-187 restrict writes and privilege escalation but do not restrict reads or network egress; `--userns=keep-id` likewise does not mitigate disclosure. Arguments are safely passed as an array, so command injection was rejected as a separate candidate, but the secret-exposure and mutable-supply-chain path remains reproducible from this file alone.
